briefings.title: Acast Q4 2025 report
briefings.tldr: Acast achieved its first-ever full year of positive operating profit and cash flow in 2025, fueled by a 61% revenue surge in the U.S. and a strategic shift toward high-margin, omni-channel "narrative influence" advertising.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Acast achieved its first-ever full year of positive operating profit and cash flow in 2025, fueled by a 61% revenue surge in the U.S. and a strategic shift toward high-margin, omni-channel "narrative influence" advertising.

## 2025 Financial Performance & U.S. Dominance
*   **Key Milestones:** For the first time since inception, Acast reported a positive full-year operating profit and cash flow.
    *   **Revenue Growth:** Full-year revenue grew 29% (33% organic). Q4 specifically saw 27% growth.
    *   **Profitability Margins:** Delivered a 5% adjusted EBITDA margin for the full year; Q4 adjusted EBIT margin reached 6%, double the previous year's 3%.
*   **The U.S. as Growth Engine:** The United States has officially become Acast’s largest market, representing 32% of total annual revenue.
    *   **U.S. Expansion:** Revenue in the region grew 61% year-over-year.
    *   **Market Position:** Management attributes U.S. success to being the "largest pure-play" provider, focusing exclusively on podcasting while competitors balance multiple media types (radio, music, etc.).
*   **Liquidity:** The company concluded the year with a robust cash position of 589 million SEK.

## Advertising Efficiency and "Quality" Metrics
*   **Monetization Levers:** While total listens remained relatively flat (1% growth), Acast significantly increased its revenue per listen by focusing on high-value inventory.
    *   **ARPL Increase:** Average Revenue Per Listen (ARPL) rose 21% to 0.66 SEK.
    *   **Inventory Capacity:** Monetizable inventory grew by 26%, and the sell-through rate improved to 43%.
*   **Premium Pricing (CPM):** Average CPM increased to $15 USD.
    *   **Driving Factors:** CFO Anders Hägg noted that pricing is being driven up by "integrated campaigns" that bundle audio with video and social assets.
    *   **Outcome-Based Selling:** CEO Greg Glenday emphasized that CPMs are "earned" through quality delivery and ad operations rather than a "transactional race to the bottom."
*   **Creator Payouts:** Acast has paid out over $550 million to creators since its inception, reinforcing its "flywheel" model where higher payouts attract better talent, which in turn attracts more advertisers.

## Strategic Acquisitions and Global Expansion
*   **German Market Entry:** Acast significantly deepened its footprint in Germany by acquiring **Wake Word Studios** (a production house) and **Podius** (an independent media planning platform).
    *   **Acast Creative Studios:** These acquisitions allow the launch of Acast Creative in Germany, joining existing hubs in the US, UK, Australia, France, and Sweden.
    *   **Synergies:** Podius will work alongside Acast’s U.S. subsidiary, Podchaser, to simplify podcast campaign planning for German agencies.
*   **Key Partnerships:** Secured an exclusive partnership with ***Le Monde*** in France, adding nearly 2 million monthly listens to the network.
*   **Market Maturity:** In November 2025, Acast moved to the Nasdaq Stockholm main market, a move management views as a validation of the company's consistency and maturity.

## Future Outlook and 2028 Targets
*   **Long-Term Guidance:** Management reiterated its 2028 targets, including a 10% EBIT margin and a revenue CAGR of 15%.
*   **Omni-channel Strategy:** The company is moving "upstream" in the planning process, solving marketing problems for Fortune 500 brands by offering narrative influence across audio, video (including YouTube/Spotify video partnerships), and live events.
*   **Operational Focus:** For 2026, the company plans to refine FX processes to mitigate unrealized currency exchange losses, which impacted the 2025 reported top line in markets like the UK.

## Notable Quotes
> "We are the largest company that just focuses on this narrative influencer market. We think this is very bespoke; it's not a subset of radio, it's not a subset of satellite... Our specialization has really allowed us to accelerate in the US." — **Greg Glenday, CEO**

> "Our focus isn't just on volume; it's on quality. We are prioritizing commercially valuable listens that drive the most value for our advertisers... Our average revenue per listen increased by 21%... an indicator of our ability to generate more value out of every single listen." — **Anders Hägg, CFO**

> "When [global brands] come to us, if they want to do transactions in audio, we're happy to do that. But that limits what you can ask for. As you work upstream... we're solving their brand problems... That unlocks much, much, much larger budgets." — **Greg Glenday, CEO**

briefings.title: Clio CEO ($400m ARR) on Moving from “classic” SaaS to AI-native
briefings.tldr: The SaaS industry is shifting from a “system of record” to a “system of action,” where AI doesn't just manage workflows but executes the work itself, potentially expanding the legal tech Total Addressable Market (TAM) from $25 billion to $1 trillion.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The SaaS industry is shifting from a “system of record” to a “system of action,” where AI doesn't just manage workflows but executes the work itself, potentially expanding the legal tech Total Addressable Market (TAM) from $25 billion to $1 trillion.

## The Shift from "System of Record" to "System of Action"
*   **Defining the Evolution:** For 17 years, Clio acted as a system of record, focusing on tracking time, billing, and document management. In the AI era, it is becoming a system of action that performs legal tasks on behalf of the user.
*   **Selling Work, Not Software:** CEO Jack Newton highlights a paradigm shift (inspired by Sarah Tavel) where the value proposition is no longer orchestration, but execution.
    *   **TAM Expansion:** Moving from selling software ($20-25B market) to selling the execution of legal services ($1T global market).
*   **KPI Transformation:** In a system of action, traditional metrics like Daily Active Users (DAU) or Monthly Active Users (MAU) may become counter-intuitive.
    *   **Efficiency over Engagement:** Success may look like *reduced* time spent in the app because AI agents are automating the "toil," allowing lawyers to focus on high-level strategy.
    *   **Value-Based Metrics:** Clio is shifting focus to quantifying time saved, revenue generated for the firm, and "first-shot" accuracy of AI answers.

## Comparing the Cloud Revolution to the AI Era
*   **Adoption Velocity:** Newton notes that the legal industry's transition to the cloud took roughly a decade; the adoption of AI is moving at 10x that speed, with a year's worth of progress matching a previous decade.
*   **Market Pull vs. Push:** In 2008, Clio had to "push" the cloud to skeptical lawyers who viewed it as a malpractice risk. Today, lawyers are "pulling" AI into their practices, recognizing it as an existential necessity.
*   **Educational Requirements:** Similar to the early cloud days, the current hurdle is education. Clio is investing heavily in "thought leadership" to help lawyers navigate the ethics of LLMs, such as managing hallucinations and maintaining professional responsibility.

## Vertical SaaS and Enterprise Strategy
*   **The Vertical Advantage:** Newton believes vertical SaaS founders have a greater opportunity than horizontal providers because they can deeply automate niche industry workflows (e.g., specific AI tools for IP litigation vs. personal injury).
*   **Enterprise Expansion:** Clio is aggressively moving upmarket with "Clio for Enterprise" to replace antiquated on-premise systems.
    *   **The Infrastructure Hierarchy:** Firms cannot achieve AI ambitions without first moving data to the cloud. Enterprise law firms are realizing their legacy on-premise tech is a blocker to AI adoption.
*   **Strategic M&A:** Clio uses its ecosystem of 300+ integration partners as a "proving ground" for acquisitions. 
    *   Five of Clio's six acquisitions (including Vlex and Sharedo) were previously integration partners, allowing Clio to see real-world usage data before buying.

## Leadership and Founder Resilience
*   **Managing Psychology:** Newton emphasizes that building a company to $400M ARR involves "devastating lows" and periods of near-failure. He credits "pathological optimism" and having a co-founder as essential for survival.
*   **Customer Obsession:** Advice for new founders is to focus on making a product indispensable for one customer, then ten, rather than focusing on scale prematurely. 
*   **Personal Discipline:** To manage the intensity of the CEO role, Newton has maintained a running streak of over 27 years (approx. 10,000 days), running at least 2km every single day without exception. He views this as essential meditative time for reflection and prioritization.

## Notable Quotes

> "AI is not going to replace lawyers, but lawyers leveraging AI are going to replace those that are not." — **Jack Newton**

> "What we saw take a decade with cloud in terms of adoption is happening in a year in AI terms. That's without any sense of hyperbole; that's literally what our data shows." — **Jack Newton**

> "The real value of AI is not doing what SaaS has typically done, which is help people manage their work and orchestrate their work, but it’s actually in doing the work." — **Jack Newton**

> "History does not repeat itself, but it does rhyme. What we're seeing with the AI era versus the cloud era is that it certainly rhymes... but the pace of change has been increased by an order of magnitude." — **Jack Newton**

briefings.title: Elon Reveals xAI & SpaceX Masterplan (Full speech from today)
briefings.tldr: xAI is rapidly scaling toward 1 million H100-equivalent GPUs to power a "recursive self-improvement" loop across four core pillars: Grok, Coding, Imagine, and MacroHard.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
xAI is rapidly scaling toward 1 million H100-equivalent GPUs to power a "recursive self-improvement" loop across four core pillars: Grok, Coding, Imagine, and MacroHard. The company aims to transition from Earth-based supercomputers to orbital and lunar data centers to achieve the massive energy required for "Encyclopedia Galactica."

## Product Pillars and the "MacroHard" Vision
- **MacroHard (Digital Emulation):** Positioned as the company’s most important project, aimed at the full digital emulation of entire human companies.
    - Focuses on "digital-output" industries (e.g., software, chip design, rocket engineering).
    - Goal: A human emulator capable of using any computer tool 24/7 without intervention.
- **Coding and Recursive Self-Improvement:** The team is targeting "singularity" in coding through a path of exponential takeoff.
    - **Binary Generation:** Musk predicts that by the end of 2025, AI will bypass traditional coding and compilers to generate optimized binaries directly.
    - Current Grok models are already used to debug and train the next generation of Grok code.
- **Imagine (Visual Generation):** xAI claims to lead the industry in volume, generating 50 million videos per day and 6 billion images per month.
    - **Future Roadmap:** Development of 10–20 minute video generation and real-time world rendering where users interact with AI-generated environments.
- **Grok Main and Grockipedia:** Shifting away from "internet evals" to "expert tutors" (doctors, lawyers, engineers) to verify truthfulness.
    - Grockipedia aims to surpass Wikipedia’s 7 million articles to become a distillation of all human knowledge.

## Infrastructure and Memphis Supercomputer
- **Compute Dominance:** xAI achieved the first 100,000 H100 GPU cluster and is moving toward a 1 million H100-equivalent training environment.
    - **Memphis "Colossus":** The facility currently features 300,000 GB300 platforms and will eventually scale north of 1 gigawatt (GW) of power.
    - **Vertical Integration:** The team manages everything from mechanical/electrical engineering to the custom "JAX" stack and low-level kernels to squeeze "every last drop" of performance.
- **Hardware Efficiency:** The site includes the world’s largest Tesla Megapack system for power smoothing and achieved record-breaking deployment speeds (6 weeks for major data halls).

## The X Ecosystem and Financial Services
- **X App Metrics:** The platform reached $1 billion in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) from subscriptions, with first-time downloads up 50% month-over-month.
- **X Money:** Moving into limited external beta soon, intended to be a global "central source of all monetary transactions," including mortgages, stocks, and crypto.
- **X Chat:** A standalone, fully encrypted messaging app is launching soon to compete with WhatsApp/Telegram, featuring video calls and desktop sharing.
- **Open Source Commitment:** xAI plans to open-source the recommendation algorithm and the X Chat code to ensure transparency and security.

## The Off-World Roadmap (SpaceX Integration)
- **Orbital Data Centers:** To bypass Earth's energy constraints, SpaceX and xAI are planning orbital data centers capable of 100–200 GW per year.
- **Lunar Mass Driver:** A long-term strategic goal involves building factories on the moon to manufacture AI satellites.
    - **Deep Space Launch:** A "mass driver" (rail gun) on the moon would launch these satellites into deep space to explore the universe and utilize a larger percentage of the sun's energy.
- **Strategic Merger:** The transcript highlights that SpaceX recently acquired xAI to align the goals of "understanding the universe" with "extending the light of consciousness to the stars."

## Notable Quotes
> "Things will move maybe even by the end of this year to where you don't even bother doing coding—the AI just creates the binary directly... and it can create a much more efficient binary than can be done by any compiler." — Elon Musk on the future of software engineering.

> "When you look at the most valuable companies in the world, their output is digital... It should be possible to completely emulate any company where the output is digital. This will usher in an age of prosperity which we could barely imagine." — Elon Musk on the MacroHard project.

> "I can't imagine anything more epic than a mass driver on the moon and a self-sustaining city on the moon and then going beyond the moon to Mars... This is the path to making it happen." — Elon Musk on the xAI/SpaceX mission.

briefings.title: European Innovation & Tech Summit | Keynote on Responsible AI
briefings.tldr: As AI shifts from a passive tool to an autonomous "agentic" system, organizations must move beyond the vague concept of "trust" toward active human responsibility.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
As AI shifts from a passive tool to an autonomous "agentic" system, organizations must move beyond the vague concept of "trust" toward active human responsibility. Leadership must implement a "Responsibility License" to ensure that humans—not machines or dashboards—own the outcomes of AI-driven trajectories.

## The Boardroom Dilemma: Fragmented Responsibility
In most organizations, "Responsible AI" is a fractured concept, with different departments owning only small pieces of the whole, leading to a "soup of contradictory descriptions" for the CEO.
*   **The Silo Effect:**
    *   **Legal:** Focuses solely on regulatory compliance.
    *   **Risk:** Prioritizes assessment and mitigation.
    *   **Technical/Data:** Focuses on robustness and minimizing "hallucinations."
    *   **Ethics:** Concerned with human dignity and values.
    *   **Sustainability:** Evaluates the environmental impact.
*   **The "Green Dashboard" Trap:** Even when every department’s specific metric is "green," the system can still fail. For example, a bank might inadvertently discriminate against a customer even if the data, legal, and business dashboards all report success.

## Trust vs. Responsibility: A Crucial Distinction
Karine Ysebrant de Lendonck argues that "trust" is an insufficient metric for high-stakes AI deployment because it is passive and relational.
*   **Trust as a Feeling:** Trust is based on past history and expectations (e.g., "I trust the sun will rise"). It is a passive state that offers no recourse when a system fails.
*   **Responsibility as a Commitment:** Unlike trust, responsibility is an active moral commitment. It involves "owning the future outcome even if we don't know what that outcome will be."
*   **The Failure of Trust:** If a self-driving car hits a pedestrian, telling the family "we trusted the algorithm" is an empty, meaningless statement. Responsibility requires someone to stand for the decision before it is made.

## The Shift to Agentic AI
AI is no longer just a recommendation tool; it has become "agentic," meaning it executes long chains of actions autonomously, making the traditional "human-in-the-loop" model obsolete.
*   **From Moments to Trajectories:** In the past, a human could review an AI recommendation (a "moment" of decision). Today, agentic AI manages entire "trajectories"—such as rerouting supply chains, canceling orders, and paying fees—at a speed humans cannot cognitively follow.
*   **The End of the Loop:** Because machines perform hundreds of decisions a minute, humans can no longer stay "on the loop" for every step. Companies must adapt to governing the *trajectory* rather than the individual decision.

## Three Drifts of Misplaced Responsibility
When companies operate in the "grey zone" between humans and machines, they risk three primary types of failure:
*   **Fragmentation:** Different teams look at isolated dashboards, allowing harm (like discrimination) to occur while everyone believes they are succeeding.
*   **Metrics Replacing Judgment:** Algorithms optimized for specific metrics can lack context. 
    *   *Example:* A social media algorithm designed to block 99% of violent content might inadvertently suppress historical news or war reporting because it lacks human judgment.
*   **Shift to the Aftermath:** A dangerous "we'll fix it later" mindset. While software can be "patched," real-world agentic AI cannot "reboot" a patient who received the wrong medication or a pedestrian hit by an autonomous vehicle.

## The Framework: The "Responsibility License"
To avoid the "Triangle of Strategic Failure," leadership must treat responsibility as a mandate for governing permission rather than just controlling models.
*   **Grant:** Upstream definition of boundaries. Clearly state what the AI is and is not allowed to do before deployment.
*   **Guard:** Ongoing animation of the conditions required to stay responsible while the AI is active.
*   **Pull (The Kill Switch):** The absolute necessity of a "revocable" permission. A specific human leader must have the documented mandate to pause or stop a system immediately when questions arise.

> "Trust is what we hope for, and responsibility is what we answer for—is what we stand for." — **Karine Ysebrant de Lendonck**

> "The breakdown in responsibility AI is not the disagreement about the goal... the thing is everyone wants AI to be responsible, but the responsibility is everywhere and nowhere at the same time." — **Karine Ysebrant de Lendonck**

> "The permission given by a human to a machine must always be revocable. If we cannot withdraw a permission fast, it means we’re not in control; and if we’re not in control, it means we’re not responsible." — **Karine Ysebrant de Lendonck**

briefings.title: Global governance of AI: How prepared is the UN?
briefings.tldr: Current international governance is fundamentally unprepared for the rapid emergence of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), necessitating a binding global treaty and a temporary pause on frontier AI development to prevent a catastrophic loss of human control.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Current international governance is fundamentally unprepared for the rapid emergence of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), necessitating a binding global treaty and a temporary pause on frontier AI development to prevent a catastrophic loss of human control.

## The Shift from Narrow AI to AGI
*   **Accelerated Timelines:** While AGI (Artificial General Intelligence) was previously thought to be decades away, researchers at frontier AI labs now estimate its arrival within 2 to 5 years; even skeptics suggest a 5-to-10-year window.
*   **Defining AGI:** Unlike current tools like ChatGPT, AGI represents systems capable of performing any intellectual task a human can do, including:
    *   Conducting scientific research and developing new technologies.
    *   Writing complex software and driving autonomous robotics.
    *   Running companies and making high-level governance decisions.
*   **Existential Risks:** Maxime Fournes argues that the "largest uncontrolled experiment in human history" is being conducted without democratic consent or a plan for failure.

## Critical Governance and Technical Barriers
*   **The Control Gap:** AI systems are trained rather than programmed, meaning developers do not fully understand their internal mechanics.
    *   **Alignment Failure:** The field of "alignment"—ensuring AI does what humans intend—is currently not on track to manage systems more intelligent than their creators.
*   **Democratic Deficit:** Strategic decisions regarding the future of humanity are currently concentrated in the hands of a few unelected individuals at a small number of private companies.
*   **Multilateral Arms Race:** Individual nations lack the autonomy to act alone because the competitive pressure to "win" the AI race creates a "race to the bottom" regarding safety and ethics.

## Proposed Policy Interventions
*   **Binding International Treaty:** Fournes advocates for a global mechanism similar to those used for nuclear weapons, biological weapons, and ozone-depleting chemicals to ensure binding international commitments.
*   **Frontier Development Pause:** A call for a temporary halt on the development of frontier systems to allow governance structures to catch up with technical capabilities.
*   **Incentivizing Specialized AI:** Governments should shift incentives away from general-purpose "frontier" models and toward:
    *   **Specialized Systems:** AI with better risk profiles designed for specific, narrow tasks.
    *   **Alignment Homework:** Forcing developers to solve the technical control problem before being allowed to scale further.

## Competitive Dynamics and Market Realities
*   **The Tipping Point:** Companies that refuse to use AI on ethical grounds face a "crushing advantage" from competitors who automate operations, creating an environment where participation in the race feels mandatory.
*   **Legislative Responsibility:** Parliamentarians are urged to re-establish market incentives that prioritize long-term safety and "aligned" systems over immediate, high-risk capabilities.
*   **The "Bad Actor" Dilemma:** Legislators noted the difficulty of governing when "bad players" may ignore international treaties, though Fournes maintains that a second-best solution of partial governance is insufficient for an existential threat.

> "We are conducting the largest uncontrolled experiment in human history and we are doing it without safeguards, without democratic consent and without a plan for what happens if something goes wrong." — **Maxime Fournes, CEO of PauseAI**

> "Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war." — **Statement signed by Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio, and hundreds of AI researchers**

> "If you control a system that can do all human intellectual labour, you control the future." — **Maxime Fournes, CEO of PauseAI**

briefings.title: Google’s AI boss made OpenAI issue code red. Now he wants to solve disease. | Titans and Disruptors
briefings.tldr: Sir Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind and Nobel laureate, is leading a strategic pivot to transform AI from a research endeavor into a "shipping engine" that aims to solve all human diseases and usher in a "new Renaissance" of radical abundance within the next 15 years.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Sir Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind and Nobel laureate, is leading a strategic pivot to transform AI from a research endeavor into a "shipping engine" that aims to solve all human diseases and usher in a "new Renaissance" of radical abundance within the next 15 years.

## The Strategic Consolidation of Google DeepMind
* **The "Engine Room" Pivot:** In 2023, Google merged its two world-class AI units—DeepMind and Google Brain—under Hassabis to consolidate talent and massive compute resources required for the "scaling era."
    * **Shipping Culture:** Hassabis has revitalized Google’s "golden era" culture by prioritizing calculated risks and high-velocity product launches, such as Gemini 3, VEO (video), and Nano Banana (imaging).
    * **Compute Strategy:** The merger was driven by the reality that even a company of Google’s scale could not support two separate frontier AI projects competing for the same hardware.
* **Founder Involvement:** Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin have returned to active roles; Brin is specifically focused on "programming in the weeds" for the Gemini models.
* **Business Impact:** This reorganization successfully addressed the "innovator’s dilemma," leading to Alphabet’s best stock performance in 2025 since 2009.

## AI for Science: Solving Disease via Isomorphic Labs
* **AlphaFold’s Scientific Legacy:** Having predicted 200 million protein structures (virtually everything known to science), DeepMind has provided this data for free to 3 million researchers globally.
* **Isomorphic Labs:** This spin-off company is applying AlphaFold-level breakthroughs to the $100B+ drug discovery industry.
    * **In Silico Revolution:** By conducting hypothesis searches digitally rather than in "wet labs," the company can be thousands of times more efficient.
    * **Pipeline Progress:** Isomorphic currently has 17 active drug programs in areas including cancer, cardiovascular health, and immunology.
    * **Strategic Partners:** High-profile collaborations are already underway with pharmaceutical giants Eli Lilly and Novartis.
    * **2026 Target:** Hassabis anticipates moving from preclinical to human clinical trials for their first AI-designed drugs by late 2025 or early 2026.

## The Future Roadmap: Agents, Glasses, and AGI
* **The "Universal Assistant":** Hassabis envisions a context-aware AI that follows users across all surfaces—browser, phone, car, and home—eliminating administrative friction.
* **Hardware Rebirth:** Smart glasses are identified as the potential "killer app" for AI, providing a visual and auditory interface for the digital assistant. 
* **Robotics Breakthroughs:** While research is ongoing, Hassabis predicts significant "breakthrough moments" in robotics over the next 18 months.
* **Timeline to AGI:** Hassabis views 2025 as the "watershed moment" where AI systems became capable enough to act as autonomous agents, delegating complex tasks rather than just generating text.

## Management Philosophy and Responsibility
* **The "Second Day" Schedule:** Hassabis manages his time by packing the office day with back-to-back meetings, then starting a creative "thinking day" from 10 PM to 4 AM.
* **Kaizen:** He applies the Japanese philosophy of continuous self-improvement to both his management style and the "learning machines" he builds.
* **Responsible Deployment:** Hassabis acknowledges the dual-purpose nature of AI; he advocates for "scientific rigor" and robustness to prevent misuse by bad actors as systems become more agentic and autonomous.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "We set out with a mission of solving intelligence and then using it to solve everything else." — **Sir Demis Hassabis**

> "If we don't disrupt ourselves, someone else will. You're better off being ahead of that and doing it on your terms." — **Sir Demis Hassabis**

> "I think medicine won't look like it does today... we’ll be in a kind of new golden era of discovery, a kind of new Renaissance." — **Sir Demis Hassabis**

briefings.title: Interview with Aron Cramer, CEO, BSR - We Don't Have Time Davos Hub
briefings.tldr: The global energy transition is currently a "multi-speed" process where significant technological gains in renewables are being undermined by geopolitical instability and corporate hesitancy; business leaders must shift focus from "effort" to measurable "achievement" by decoupling economic growth from emissions.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The global energy transition is currently a "multi-speed" process where significant technological gains in renewables are being undermined by geopolitical instability and corporate hesitancy; business leaders must shift focus from "effort" to measurable "achievement" by decoupling economic growth from emissions.

## The State of the Energy Transition
* **Multi-Speed Progress:** Aron Cramer notes that the transition is non-linear and varies significantly by region and sector.
    * While the IPCC data suggests progress is too slow, massive advances in wind, solar, and battery storage prices provide a counter-narrative of real momentum.
* **The "Carbon Law" Gap:** Johan Falk highlights that the "Carbon Law" requires halving emissions every decade starting from 2020. Currently, the global community is approximately five years behind this curve.
* **Collective Failure:** Despite individual success stories, Cramer emphasizes that "collectively we are off track." He asserts that in the context of climate change, the only grade that matters is achievement, not intent.

## Corporate Resilience and "Losing Nerve"
* **The "Off-Ramp" Risk:** While many companies stay the course, others are using current geopolitical conflicts, trade uncertainties, and the rise of AI as an "off-ramp" to retreat from climate commitments.
* **Implementation Challenges:** Cramer observes that writing a commitment is fundamentally different from achieving it. The actual execution of the energy transition is proving to be "expensive and messy" for many firms.
* **AI’s Dual Impact:** 
    * **The Downside:** The massive energy requirements of AI and hyperscale data centers are making it difficult for big tech companies to meet their emissions reduction targets.
    * **The Upside:** AI is already being used to improve energy grid efficiency by up to 20%, a feat that was impossible just a few years ago.

## "Crocodile Economics": Decoupling Growth from Emissions
* **Race to the Top:** The "Crocodile Economics" concept focuses on countries and companies that have successfully increased GDP/revenue while simultaneously driving down emissions.
* **Reconciling Boundaries:** Cramer argues that while we must respect planetary boundaries, we cannot impose social or economic boundaries on the public. 
    * Shifting the narrative from "burden sharing" to "human progress" is essential for gaining public and political buy-in.
* **Beyond GDP:** The briefing suggests moving toward an "Earth-aligned economy" that prioritizes human health, resilience, and circularity over imperfect measures like raw GDP.

## The Broader Business Context for 2026
* **Foundational Values:** Cramer and Falk agree that sustainable business cannot thrive without democracy, the rule of law, free trade, and stable international relations.
* **The Role of the Private Sector:** There is a growing movement of CEOs from the US and Asia publicly advocating for climate action and democratic stability as the essential foundations for a thriving economy.
* **Supply Chain Resilience:** Transitioning to electrification and a circular economy is increasingly viewed as a strategy for national and corporate security, reducing vulnerability to volatile fossil fuel supply chains.

> "There is no A for effort here, only an A for achievement. And collectively, we are off track."
> — **Aron Cramer**, CEO, BSR

> "The political environment has grown more difficult... for some companies, it's given them an off-ramp from climate action that perhaps they were never as fully committed to in the first place."
> — **Aron Cramer**, CEO, BSR

> "We have to respect planetary boundaries... but we cannot impose social and economic boundaries because politically that just doesn't work. We need to find a way to reconcile these two things."
> — **Aron Cramer**, CEO, BSR

briefings.title: Keeping Up With the Newsoms, California’s First Couple | The Circuit
briefings.tldr: Governor Gavin Newsom and First Partner Jennifer Siebel Newsom have positioned themselves as the primary progressive counterweight to "Trumpism," leveraging a deeply integrated political partnership to champion gender equity and tech regulation while navigating the personal tolls of high-profile leadership.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Governor Gavin Newsom and First Partner Jennifer Siebel Newsom have positioned themselves as the primary progressive counterweight to "Trumpism," leveraging a deeply integrated political partnership to champion gender equity and tech regulation while navigating the personal tolls of high-profile leadership.

## The Newsom Partnership and Political Strategy
* **"First Partner" Rebranding:** Jennifer Siebel Newsom rejected the "First Lady" title to emphasize her role as a "worker bee" and active policy collaborator, focusing specifically on gender equity and the wellbeing of families.
    * Governor Newsom acknowledges that while the title was unconventional, it accurately reflects their daily sharing of thoughts, passions, and concerns.
* **The "Mirror" Strategy:** The Governor has shifted to a "scorched earth" social media approach to combat Donald Trump, using humor and aggressive "clapbacks" to challenge the narrative.
    * **Political Risk:** Newsom justifies his provocative social media presence (e.g., depicting Trump as a pig) as a necessary "mirror" to what he views as the "blatant corruption" and "ruthless" nature of modern Republican tactics.
* **Institutional Checks:** The Newsoms view California as a critical check on federal power, highlighted by the state filing over 50 lawsuits against the Trump administration and the passage of Proposition 50 to prevent redistricting manipulation.

## Silicon Valley and the Tech "Backlash"
* **Shifting Loyalties:** Both Newsoms expressed concern over tech leaders (such as David Sacks) moving toward the political right. Jennifer characterizes this as a "dangerous" result of living in a "bubble of wealth."
* **Algorithmic Accountability:** The First Partner views current tech as a "backlash" against women's progress, citing a lack of female leadership and the "kaching, kaching" profit model derived from misinformation and hate.
* **AI Regulation:** Despite his history as a tech ally, Governor Newsom asserts a responsibility to regulate "truth and trust" in AI, focusing on protecting children from predatory algorithms rather than simple age-gating.
* **Billionaire Tax:** Governor Newsom remains staunchly opposed to a proposed billionaire tax, arguing it would have "profound" negative impacts and promising to defeat it if it reaches the ballot.

## Social Advocacy and Personal Resilience
* **The "Manosphere" Epidemic:** Jennifer Siebel Newsom has prioritized addressing a "loneliness epidemic" among young men, which she believes has been exploited by online figures like Andrew Tate and Charlie Kirk to promote dehumanizing values.
    * **Personal Impact:** The Newsoms revealed that their own son was briefly influenced by "Hustlers University" and crypto-related "get rich quick" content on his school device.
* **National Service:** The Governor proposed a one-to-two-year compulsory national service for young Americans to foster shared experiences and combat the isolation felt by the current generation.
* **Jennifer’s Background:** Her advocacy is rooted in personal tragedy (the accidental death of her sister) and her experience as a survivor of sexual assault by Harvey Weinstein, which she testified about in court.

## California’s Challenges and Future Ambitions
* **Addressing Affordability:** The Governor defends California’s high cost of living by pointing to aggressive housing reforms, $11 insulin, and wage increases for fast-food and healthcare workers.
* **2028 Speculation:** While betting pools place Newsom at the top of the 2028 Democratic pack, both Newsoms downplay national ambitions. 
    * **Family Toll:** The Governor noted the significant strain on their four children, including the need to homeschool one child due to the pressures of his public office.
    * **Focus:** He maintains that his current focus is strictly on the 2025-2026 cycle, calling 2028 talk a "sideshow."

> "He’s a T-Rex. You mate with him or he devours you." 
> — **Governor Gavin Newsom** (on Donald Trump)

> "In the entertainment industry, I obviously saw a dearth of women in positions of power and influence... similar to the political world, women may be rising in terms of our representation, but we don't have the same voice and power." 
> — **Jennifer Siebel Newsom**

> — **Governor Gavin Newsom**

> — **Governor Gavin Newsom**

briefings.title: LIVE: Undersecretary of War for A&S and Secretary of Energy Chris speak during a press conference
briefings.tldr: Undersecretary Michael Duffey and Secretary Chris Wright announced a strategic partnership to integrate energy production with defense acquisition, focusing on streamlining the "Sentinel" missile program and hardening military energy infrastructure to ensure national "energy dominance."
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Undersecretary Michael Duffey and Secretary Chris Wright announced a strategic partnership to integrate energy production with defense acquisition, focusing on streamlining the "Sentinel" missile program and hardening military energy infrastructure to ensure national "energy dominance."

## Strategic Shift: Transition to a "War" Posture
*   **Departmental Rebranding:** Undersecretary Duffey highlighted the shift from the "Department of Defense" to the "Department of War," signaling a move toward a high-readiness, combat-oriented acquisition strategy.
*   **Acquisition Speed:** The Undersecretary emphasized "radical transparency" and the removal of bureaucratic hurdles to accelerate the production of munitions and long-lead defense components.
*   **Industrial Base Expansion:** Plans were discussed to revitalize domestic manufacturing, specifically focusing on the specialized parts needed for the nuclear triad.

## Energy Dominance and National Security
*   **The Energy-Defense Nexus:** Secretary Chris Wright asserted that reliable, abundant energy—sourced primarily from oil, gas, and nuclear power—is the prerequisite for a dominant military industrial base.
*   **Grid Resilience at March ARB:** The speakers detailed plans to make March Air Reserve Base a model for energy independence, utilizing localized power generation to insulate the base from potential civilian grid failures or cyberattacks.
*   **Fossil Fuel Integration:** Wright defended the continued use of fossil fuels as essential for the logistics and operational mobility of the current fleet.

## Nuclear Modernization and the Sentinel Program
*   **Program Oversight:** A major portion of the briefing focused on the LGM-35A Sentinel program. Duffey and Wright committed to tighter interagency coordination between the Department of War and the Department of Energy’s NNSA (National Nuclear Security Administration).
*   **Cost and Schedule Stabilization:** Following previous delays, the leaders outlined a new oversight framework designed to prevent further cost overruns while maintaining the 2029 deployment goals.
*   **Warhead Production:** Secretary Wright confirmed that the DOE is scaling up its "pit" production and warhead refurbishment facilities to ensure the delivery systems are fully mission-capable.

## Workforce and Regional Impact
*   **Job Creation:** The speakers highlighted that the modernization efforts at March ARB and associated manufacturing sites will require thousands of highly skilled technicians and engineers.
*   **Public-Private Partnerships:** There is a renewed emphasis on "Defense-Private Partnerships" (DPPs) where private energy companies work directly with base commanders to manage utility infrastructure.

> "We are moving from a posture of management to a posture of production. The Department of War is open for business, and we are looking for partners who can move as fast as we do."
— **Michael Duffey**

> "Energy dominance is not just an economic goal; it is a tactical necessity. You cannot have a strong military without a massive, reliable, and affordable energy supply."
— **Chris Wright**

briefings.title: Magic Johnson on The $1B Nike Deal That Got Away | Full Conversation with a16z
briefings.tldr: Earvin "Magic" Johnson details his transition from NBA legend to billionaire businessman, emphasizing the shift from endorsement-based income to equity-driven growth, the necessity of building teams "smarter than yourself," and the immense long-term compounding value of sports assets and "boring" businesses.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Earvin "Magic" Johnson details his transition from NBA legend to billionaire businessman, emphasizing the shift from endorsement-based income to equity-driven growth, the necessity of building teams "smarter than yourself," and the immense long-term compounding value of sports assets and "boring" businesses.

## Mentorship and the Foundation of Deal-Making
*   **The Ovitz Model:** Magic credits Michael Ovitz (co-founder of CAA) for teaching him the "art of the deal."
    *   **The Rolodex:** Ovitz emphasized building a massive network of CEOs and power players, noting that you might not need a contact today, but you will need them tomorrow.
    *   **Early is On-Time:** A key professional habit learned from billionaire mentors is arriving early to meetings; the most successful people value their time and often conduct the best business before the official start time.
*   **Dr. Jerry Buss:** The former Lakers owner served as Magic’s first business mentor, treating him like a son while insisting he "write a check" to have skin in the game for his first ownership stakes.
*   **Relationship Longevity:** Magic notes that many of his most successful partnerships, such as with Ron Burkle (Yucaipa), were built over a decade of friendship before a formal deal was signed.

## Investment Philosophy: Equity vs. Endorsements
*   **The "One That Got Away":** In 1979, Nike co-founder Phil Knight offered Magic stock because the company lacked the cash for a traditional endorsement. Magic turned it down for cash.
    *   **The Cost:** Recent analytics suggest that the stock would be worth over **$1 billion** today.
*   **Boring Businesses:** Magic and Chris Lyons discuss how "boring" businesses—like insurance, movie theaters, and food service—are often superior to trendy startups.
    *   **The Starbucks Success:** Partnering with Howard Schultz to bring 125 Starbucks stores to urban markets proved that minority communities had massive, untapped spending power ($1.4 trillion to $2 trillion collectively).
*   **Transitioning to Equity:** Magic highlights that the next generation of athletes (LeBron James, Steph Curry, Kevin Durant) has successfully pivoted from "getting a check" to owning the brands and teams they represent.

## The Business of Sports Ownership
*   **Asset Appreciation:** Magic highlights the explosive growth in sports team valuations:
    *   **L.A. Dodgers:** Purchased for $2.2 billion (at the time considered an overpayment); currently valued at $8 billion.
    *   **Washington Commanders:** Purchased for $6 billion; already trending toward an $8 billion valuation with a new stadium in development.
    *   **L.A. Sparks/WNBA:** Magic invested when the league was "losing money," but the asset has since skyrocketed to a ~$300 million valuation due to increased fan interest and TV contracts.
*   **The Fan Experience:** A core tenet of Magic’s ownership strategy is investing hundreds of millions into stadium infrastructure and player development. He argues that you must "spend money to make money" to justify rising ticket prices to the fans.
*   **Analytics in Sports:** Modern winning requires a heavy investment in data and analytics—a shift from Magic’s playing days where instinct ruled.

## Building a Professional Infrastructure
*   **Hire Intelligence:** Magic’s primary advice to entertainers and athletes is to hire people "smarter than yourself" and pay them well to conduct business while the talent is "on stage" or "on the court."
*   **The Power of "No":** A successful team must include advisors who are willing to tell the principal "no" regarding bad deals or lifestyle spending.
*   **Collaborative Abundance:** Magic encourages the "myth" of the solo entrepreneur to be discarded, emphasizing that partnering and sharing knowledge is the only way to build multi-generational wealth within minority communities.

## Technology and the Future
*   **Skydio and Early Tech:** Magic was an early investor in Skydio (autonomous drones) 10 years ago, recognizing the potential for AI and autonomy in sports and defense before it became mainstream.
*   **AI Efficiency:** Magic views AI as a tool to lower costs and increase speed across all industries, citing his recent investments in Alchemy Health and Function Health as examples of tech-driven disruption in the pharmacy and bio sectors.
*   **Investment Signal:** When evaluating tech deals, Magic looks at the lead investor (e.g., a16z). He treats a lead investor’s track record as a primary filter for vetting the deal's viability.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "Phil Knight said, 'I don’t have the money they have, but I got stock.' ...If I had done that deal in 1979, it’d be over a billion dollars. That’s the one that got away." — **Magic Johnson**

> "Get people who are smarter than yourself, get the right people, and always pay them—and then let them do their thing." — **Magic Johnson**

> "Boring businesses keep—that’s a secret. Everybody wants to find the hottest company... but the ones that are boring and people don't know about are the ones consistently making money." — **Chris Lyons**

> "The downfall of minorities has been most of the rich people before us took the knowledge with them. They didn't share it. I want people to know this is the man [Chris Lyons] right here." — **Magic Johnson**

briefings.title: Meet The Former Tech Executive Using SaaS Strategies To Scale Professional Women’s Football
briefings.tldr: The Women’s National Football Conference (WNFC) is a 16-team professional tackle football league transitioning from a bootstrapped startup to a $50 million Series A funding round, utilizing lean SaaS business strategies to achieve profitability and financial equity for female athletes.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The Women’s National Football Conference (WNFC) is a 16-team professional tackle football league transitioning from a bootstrapped startup to a $50 million Series A funding round, utilizing lean SaaS business strategies to achieve profitability and financial equity for female athletes.

## Financial Strategy and Scaling
* **SaaS Methodology:** Founder Odessa Jenkins applied mechanisms from her tech background to grow the league leanly and efficiently, prioritizing market building over early external investment.
* **Funding Rounds:**
    * **Bootstrapping:** The league operated for its first 4–5 years using internal revenue from apparel and ticket sales.
    * **Seed Round:** Raised $1.5 million at a $20 million valuation in late 2024, led by investor and CEO Dot Sherman.
    * **Series A:** The league is currently launching a Series A round with a target valuation of $50 million.
* **Profitability:** The business is currently profitable due to a lean operating model, with revenue quadrupling annually in key areas.

## League Structure and Valuation
* **Equity Model:** The WNFC is a private corporation where the 16 individual team owners also hold equity in the league. This "team-owned entity" structure allows investors to buy in at the league level or the team level.
* **Franchise Values:** Individual team valuations currently range between $1 million and $3 million.
* **Market Strategy:**
    * **Current Footprint:** Operating in major markets including Los Angeles, Las Vegas, Chicago, Dallas, and New Jersey.
    * **Expansion:** Jenkins plans to cap the league at 16–20 teams to avoid the pitfalls of over-expansion, with interest in North Carolina and Arizona.
    * **Selection Criteria:** Focuses on the quality and longevity of ownership groups rather than just geographic location.

## Revenue Diversification and Media
* **The Revenue Pie:** Financials are heavily weighted toward national sponsorships (Adidas, Dove, Riddell) and a vertically integrated apparel business.
* **Media Rights:**
    * **Victory Plus:** A five-year deal provides a consistent streaming home alongside other major sports like the NWSL and MLB.
    * **Linear Reach:** The 2024 championship debuted on ESPN2, reaching 150,000 households and 20,000 simultaneous streamers.
* **Social Engagement:** The league engaged approximately 100 million people across Meta platforms last year, a metric they aim to convert into increased viewership and streaming numbers.

## Athlete Compensation and Player Safety
* **Transitioning Pay Scales:** Players currently earn via performance bonuses and local sponsorships. The Series A capital is intended to shift the league toward a "living wage" or regular game-day salary model.
* **Safety Protocols:**
    * **NFL Standards:** The league "copycatted" NFL head and neck safety protocols, utilizing Sway Medical for baseline concussion testing.
    * **Coaching Certification:** 100% of WNFC coaching staff is CPR and first-aid certified.
* **The Role of Flag Football:** Jenkins views the rise of flag football (and its Olympic inclusion) as a "pipeline driver" rather than a competitor. NFL and NCAA investment in flag has grown the WNFC’s business by 100% by increasing overall female participation in the sport.

> "Our singular goal is to build a profitable business to get women paid to play professional tackle football." — **Odessa Jenkins**

> "We had to figure it out by building a market first and then building a business... by the time we were able to attract a seed investor, we had a really strong business." — **Odessa Jenkins**

> "Flag is a part of football. You call it what you want to call it... it’s done wonders for the business of the WNFC." — **Odessa Jenkins**

briefings.title: Metrology as a driver for the industrial revolution | Keynote by Dr Nathalie von Siemens
briefings.tldr: Metrology serves as the foundational science for both the Industrial and Digital Revolutions, providing the precision, standardization, and international cooperation necessary to scale technological innovation for the benefit of humanity.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Metrology serves as the foundational science for both the Industrial and Digital Revolutions, providing the precision, standardization, and international cooperation necessary to scale technological innovation for the benefit of humanity.

## Metrology as the Engine of Industrialization
Dr. Nathalie von Siemens identifies metrology as the prerequisite for technical progress, transforming industrial production from artisanal craft to a globalized system.
* **Standardization and Interchangeability:** Metrology allowed for the creation of identical parts, ensuring components matched regardless of where they were produced.
* **Mass Production Efficiency:** Precise measurement enabled the rapid adjustment of machinery for serial production, a hallmark of the Industrial Revolution.
* **Quality Control:** Dimensions and tolerances could be checked systematically, identifying defects and reducing non-conformity.
* **Global Trade Facilitation:** The introduction of the metric system and the Metre Convention established a common language for international trade, supporting the global spread of products.

## The Revolutionary Legacy of the PTB
The speaker highlights her ancestors, Werner von Siemens and Hermann von Helmholtz, as "revolutionaries" who recognized that scientific measurement was essential for industrial application.
* **The Physikalisch-Technische Reichsanstalt (PTB):** Founded as the first German public-private partnership for science, the PTB broke down silos by combining basic research with industrial technology.
* **The Indo-European Telegraph:** To successfully lay a line from London to Calcutta, Werner von Siemens required "plug-and-play" cables and reliable electrical standards. 
    * **Impact:** This standardization reduced communication time from 30 days to 30 minutes.
* **Quantum Foundations:** The revolutionary setup of the PTB later enabled breakthrough measurements that led to quantum technology based on Max Planck’s theories.

## Driving the Digital Revolution through Standardization
The same principles that drove the age of steam and electricity are now fueling the digital era, specifically through nano-level precision and market-defining standards.
* **EUV Lithography:** High-performance microchips—the heart of the digital revolution—rely on precision metrology at the nano level.
* **Market Receptiveness:** Standardization increases the acceptance of innovations and provides investment security.
    * **Smart Grids:** The market for digitalized power equipment only opened significantly after the establishment of the **IEC 61850** standards.
    * **Cybersecurity:** Breakthroughs in SCADA and OT system security were enabled by the **IEC 62443** standards.

## Recognizing Scientific Excellence
Dr. von Siemens emphasizes that "changemakers" require encouragement, highlighting two major awards that bridge the gap between discovery and application.
* **The Helmholtz Award:** Honors outstanding work in precision measurement across physics, chemistry, and medicine.
    * **2024 Winners:** Awarded to Professor Baum for capturing atomic movements using microscopy, and a team led by Professor Roth and Professor Emmert for optical biopsy in skin cancer diagnostics.
* **The Werner-von-Siemens-Ring:** Regarded as the "Nobel Prize in technical sciences."
    * **2024 Winners:** Awarded to Peter Kurz (Zeiss) and Michael Kaschke (Trumpf) for their industrial utilization of EUV technology.

## Ethical Complexity and Future Sustainability
While revolutions bring progress, they also introduce social and environmental challenges that require a data-driven, scientific approach to solve.
* **Addressing Past and Present Failures:** The Industrial Revolution led to "pauperism" and the climate crisis; the Digital Revolution faces fears of job displacement and geopolitical tension.
* **Data-Driven Solutions:** The speaker argues that the climate crisis can be mitigated through "smart cities" built on sensor networks, optimizing energy from renewables and improving mobility.
* **Global Collaboration:** Science and art remain the "bond of peace among nations," requiring a diverse, international team to work for the common benefit of all.

> "Metrology is doubtless the basic science of the Industrial Revolution. And I am convinced metrology is also a key for the digital revolution." — **Dr. Nathalie von Siemens**

> "Science and art are currently the only remaining bond of peace among nations. Their ever-increasing development is a common goal of all, to be pursued in the common work of all for the common benefit of all." — **Hermann von Helmholtz (quoted by Dr. von Siemens)**

> "Standardization is the key to conquering new markets... Standards offer investment security and boost the acceptance of innovation." — **Dr. Nathalie von Siemens**

briefings.title: Microsoft and Software Survival | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Microsoft is navigating a fundamental shift where AI-written code commoditizes software, forcing a transition from "growing the pie" to a predatory battle for industry adjacencies.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Microsoft is navigating a fundamental shift where AI-written code commoditizes software, forcing a transition from "growing the pie" to a predatory battle for industry adjacencies. To survive, Microsoft is prioritizing its own high-margin AI agents and R&D over third-party Azure demand, signaling a strategic pivot toward "Work IQ" and integrated utility.

## The Software Survival Crisis
*   **The End of the SaaS Golden Age:** The previous decade of SaaS focused on identifying a business function and building a siloed app. AI-written code collapses this model by lowering the cost of code to near-zero, enabling every software company to attack their neighbors' territory.
*   **Commoditization Risks:** While businesses are unlikely to write all their own software, the abundance of AI-generated code means software companies must justify their existence through support, compliance, and integrations rather than just the code itself.
*   **A Zero-Sum Market:** Companies are increasingly cutting software spend to fund their own AI token usage. This shifts the software industry from a period of expansion to a "fight for the pie," where the primary survivors will be those who can leverage AI to rapidly absorb adjacent business functions.

## The Azure Miss and Capacity Prioritization
*   **Financial Impact:** Microsoft experienced its biggest stock plunge since 2020, losing $357 billion in value in a single session—second only to Nvidia’s rout following the DeepSeek launch. 
*   **Strategic Resource Allocation:** The reported "miss" in Azure growth (which fell 1% below expectations) was a deliberate choice. CFO Amy Hood confirmed that Microsoft prioritized GPU capacity for internal R&D and first-party apps like M365 Copilot and GitHub Copilot over renting that capacity to Azure customers.
*   **High-Margin Preference:** CEO Satya Nadella defended this "portfolio approach," noting that Microsoft earns better margins and higher Lifetime Value (LTV) from its own productivity applications than from pure cloud infrastructure.
*   **Infrastructure Stress:** Capital expenditures reached a record $37.5 billion in the most recent quarter, a 66% year-over-year increase, highlighting the extreme costs of maintaining the AI lead.

## Work IQ and the Future of Agents
*   **The Identity Advantage:** Microsoft’s "Work IQ" strategy leverages its ownership of identity (Active Directory) to build agents that understand a worker’s role, communications, and history.
*   **The Per-Seat Licensing Risk:** Microsoft’s current business model relies heavily on per-seat licensing. As AI agents begin to perform the work of humans, the number of "seats" may dwindle, threatening the company's core revenue stream.
*   **Adjacency as Defense:** To counter the shrinking per-seat market, Microsoft is aggressively incorporating more business functions into its suite. The goal is to make its agents more capable and the software surface area so large that other software makers are forced to interface with Microsoft’s ecosystem.

## The Rise of "Token Foundries"
*   **The Integrated Fab Problem:** Azure currently operates like an "Integrated Device Manufacturer" (e.g., Intel), where it builds the infrastructure but prioritizes its own products during shortages. 
*   **Customer Conflict:** Azure customers (including OpenAI, which represents 45% of Azure’s Remaining Performance Obligations) are effectively "last in line" behind Microsoft's internal needs.
*   **Market Opportunity:** This creates a strategic opening for "pure play" token foundries—like Oracle or specialized "neoclouds"—that do not compete with their customers and can offer guaranteed capacity, similar to the TSMC model in semiconductors.

> "The software giant’s stock closed down 10%, its biggest plunge since March 2020... following Microsoft’s earnings after the bell Wednesday, which showed record spending on artificial intelligence as growth at its key cloud unit slowed." — **Bloomberg Report**

> "If I had taken the GPUs that just came online in Q1 and Q2 in terms of GPUs and allocated them all to Azure, the KPI would have been over 40... this is about investing in all the layers of the stack that benefit customers." — **Amy Hood, Microsoft CFO**

> "We don’t want to maximize just 1 business of ours, we want to be able to allocate capacity, while we’re sort of supply constrained in a way that allow us to essentially build the best LTV portfolio." — **Satya Nadella, Microsoft CEO**

briefings.title: Mike Gitlin - CEO of Capital Group | Podcast | In Good Company | Norges Bank Investment Management
briefings.tldr: Capital Group maintains its status as a "gold standard" in investment management by utilizing a unique multi-manager system, prioritizing an eight-year incentive horizon to eliminate short-termism, and operating under a 94-year-old employee-owned structure that ensures intergenerational stability.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Capital Group maintains its status as a "gold standard" in investment management by utilizing a unique multi-manager system, prioritizing an eight-year incentive horizon to eliminate short-termism, and operating under a 94-year-old employee-owned structure that ensures intergenerational stability.

## The "Capital System" Investment Model
* **The Multi-Manager Approach:** Launched in 1958 to eliminate "key person risk," the system divides portfolios among multiple managers and analysts rather than a single individual.
    * **The Principal Investment Officer (PIO):** Acts as the "conductor of the orchestra," ensuring accountability while allowing various managers to express their highest-conviction ideas.
    * **Analysts as Investors:** Unlike many firms where analysts merely rate stocks, Capital Group analysts manage real client assets. This "skin in the game" forces them to understand portfolio risk and diversification.
* **Style Consistency:** The firm prioritizes managers who avoid "style creep." Gitlin emphasizes that even in bull markets, managers must stick to their defined styles (growth, value, etc.) so that the overall portfolio risk remains intended and balanced.
* **Low Attrition:** The average tenure for portfolio managers exceeds 20 years, with investment professional attrition in the low single digits.

## Long-Termism and Compensation Structure
* **8-Year Incentive Horizon:** The primary driver of quantitative compensation is an investment professional's rolling 8-year performance record, followed by 5-year and 3-year windows.
    * **Reducing Volatility:** By making the 1-year number the smallest component of compensation, the firm discourages "hedge fund" behavior and reactive, knee-jerk decision-making.
* **The "Time" Edge:** Gitlin argues that the firm’s competitive advantage is simply *time*—the ability to stay with a thesis and go against the grain without fear of quarterly reprisal.
* **Client Alignment:** This structure mirrors the goals of their 20 million+ family clients who are saving for retirement decades in the future, rather than focusing on the 24-hour news cycle.

## Strategic Evolution: AI, Passive Markets, and Private Equity
* **Active vs. Passive Dynamics:** Gitlin notes that as passive management reaches ~50% of the market, benchmarks have become dangerously concentrated. This creates a massive opportunity for active managers to provide true diversification by looking at the "53,000+ public companies" outside the top few.
* **AI and Proprietary Data:** Capital Group is leveraging AI to mine 94 years of digitized proprietary research.
    * **Investor Insights:** AI tools help current investors analyze their past decisions in similar market cycles to identify recurring mistakes or successes.
    * **Efficiency:** Automated tools like "Prep Me" help advisors synthesize client notes and history for more productive interactions.
* **Hybrid Private Markets:** Rather than building or buying a private equity arm, Capital Group partnered with KKR.
    * **Avoiding "Practice":** Gitlin stated they were unwilling to "practice" on client money while learning the private space; partnering allows them to combine KKR’s 50 years of expertise with Capital’s public market scale.

## Culture and Ownership Structure
* **"Rented" Ownership:** The firm is 100% employee-owned, but Gitlin describes it as "rented." Owners must sell their shares back to the firm upon retirement.
    * **Anti-Concentration:** No single individual owns more than approximately 1% of the firm, ensuring that the incentive is to pass a healthy business to the next generation rather than monetize for personal gain.
* **The Hiring "Veto":** The recruitment process is intentionally slow, lasting 6 to 12 months. This ensures cultural fit and helps candidates determine if they are truly ready for a career-long commitment.
* **In-Person Collaboration:** The firm maintains a four-day in-office week, citing that face-to-face verbal communication is superior to virtual collaboration for deep investment debate.

## Notable Quotes
> **Mike Gitlin:** "The number one driver of an analyst or portfolio manager's quantitative compensation is their 8-year number... it says don't be a hedge fund manager. Manage for the long term."

> **Mike Gitlin:** "We like to talk about writing a chapter in the Capital Group book and then passing it on for someone else to write the chapter... it’s a really interesting mentality of the life cycle of a company."

> **Mike Gitlin (on the KKR partnership):** "To build it ourselves, you would then have to be willing to practice on your clients' money, right? Because you don't have [the expertise] yet. We weren't willing to do that."

> **Mike Gitlin:** "I like to say there's 53,007 public companies, there's not seven public companies. Having the opportunity to move away from the skewed benchmark and find opportunities outside of that... is a great advantage for active managers."

people.name: Scott Bessent
people.role: 79th Secretary of the Treasury, United States

briefings.tldr: The U.S. is pursuing a "growth-first" economic solution characterized by aggressive deregulation, re-industrialization through strategic tariffs, and a generational pivot toward Latin American partnerships to ensure global stability and economic sovereignty.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The U.S. is pursuing a "growth-first" economic solution characterized by aggressive deregulation, re-industrialization through strategic tariffs, and a generational pivot toward Latin American partnerships to ensure global stability and economic sovereignty.

## U.S. Fiscal Policy and Growth Strategy
* **The "Growth Solution":** Secretary Bessent emphasizes that high growth—not just austerity—is the primary path to financial stability.
    * **Deficit Targets:** The administration aims to reduce the deficit-to-GDP ratio to below 4% ("something with a 3 in front of it") by the end of the term to stabilize debt and encourage deleveraging.
    * **Deregulation:** A major shift in the regulatory environment is underway, with Bessent reporting a ratio of 23 regulations cut for every one new regulation introduced.
    * **Non-inflationary Growth:** By coupling tax-driven demand with supply-side deregulation (energy dominance and manufacturing space), the administration believes it can achieve ~4% growth without spiking inflation.

## Re-industrialization and Tariff Philosophy
* **The "Shrinking Ice Cube" Analogy:** Bessent describes tariff policy as a transitional tool for rebalancing the economy.
    * **Revenue Shift:** While initial tariff revenues are high, the long-term goal is to replace that income with corporate tax revenue from new domestic factories and reshored jobs.
    * **FDI and Tax Certainty:** The "July 4th" bill, which includes full expensing for corporations, is designed to make the U.S. the most attractive destination for global capital.
* **Energy Sovereignty:** A core pillar of the strategy involves exploiting natural resources, including "clean coal," crude oil, and natural gas, to provide energy certainty for manufacturers.

## The Productivity Boom and AI
* **Return to the 1990s:** Bessent draws parallels between the current AI-driven era and the productivity boom of the 1990s.
* **Federal Reserve Leadership:** He highlights the appointment of Kevin Warsh as Fed Chairman, noting Warsh’s "open mind" regarding productivity gains and his background in technology investment.
* **Labor Reallocation:** Rather than mass unemployment, Bessent anticipates an "internal reallocation" of labor. 
    * **AI Natives:** He urges young workers to become "AI natives," similar to the "digital natives" of the 2000s, to capitalize on the shifting job market.

## Geopolitics: Latin America and Global Rebalancing
* **Latin America as a Generational Opportunity:** The administration is prioritizing a "North-South" focus, citing the region's cultural fit, shared time zones, and vast natural resources.
    * **Argentina:** Bessent highlights U.S. support for President Milei as a "peace through economic strength" bridge during his election.
    * **Venezuela:** The extradition of Nicolas Maduro is cited as a demonstration of U.S. military power facilitating a return to free and fair elections.
    * **Brazil:** Despite a "rocky start," Bessent notes a positive rapport between Presidents Trump and Lula, expressing optimism for future business delegations.
* **China and Europe:**
    * **De-risking, not Decoupling:** The U.S. seeks a "fair rivalry" with China but insists on reclaiming sovereignty in strategic industries (semiconductors, medicines, minerals).
    * **Critique of Europe:** Bessent views the EU as "stifling growth" through over-regulation and advises European leaders to follow the "Draghi report" to restore productivity.

## Notable Quotes

* **Permitting Breakthrough:** President Trump announced that his administration has approved over 70 permits for major coal mining projects in one year, contrasting this with zero approvals under the previous administration.

* **Performance During Extremes:** During recent winter storms, coal generation surged by 31% to meet demand, while the President claimed solar and wind energy "collapsed."
